This is a Frigidaire part, and it was exactly what I had originally.  No more E64 error from the dryer.  There are a couple of DIY websites that walk a person through replacing the heater, and I highly recommend looking at them.  The replacement took me a couple of hours, which also involved getting the vacuum out and cleaning all the dust bunnies.  There are about 50 screws that have to be removed and reinstalled, and like most repairs there's one that's really hard to get to, the one on the heater mount on the side of the dryer.  The screws are square-headed, so make sure you have the right screw driver before you start.  A Phillips head will kind of work, but I don't recommend it.  Oh, and check the part before you start.  Amazon sent the wrong part the first time.  I didn't realize it until I tried to connect the new part and there wasn't 4 electrical connections.  Amazon was good about it though, I got the right part the very next day, on a Sunday.

I watched a few youtube videos on the E64 error i was getting, and was able to deduce that the heater needed to be replaced.  Next was figuring out if this was something I could fix myself, and after viewing a few videos on youtube, I decided to tackle the job.  First piece of advice is to ensure you've got room to work with...either behind the dryer or the front.  (there are videos on how to address the issue from either side).  I chose to go through the back.  Lots and lots of screw to take out to the the top panel, back panel, and other pieces off.  90% of the screws are the same, with a few variations that you'll need to make note of.  About three quarters of the way through disassembly, I was starting to question my motives, but after coming to my senses, I was able to remove the old heater, and it was filthy and obvious the culprit when compared to the new unit. The quality of this replacement part is about the same as the part that came with the dryer: It sucks. There is no other way to put it. The center plenum has 90° lips bent on them to limit warping - but the anti-warp lip is only on the center 1/3 of the plenum. So, the hot end of the plenum twists and distorts until the heating element grounds out against the housing (bad). In my case, I had TWO elements 'self-ground' so my only heating option was 'high' as all three elements were 'on' any time I ran the dryer. The overall electrical design and mechanical implementation is very, very poor. Would much rather have my old Kenmore dryer - lasted 30 years. During that time, I had to replace the heating element twice (once at 10 years, once at 20 years). Short product lifetime rooted in a terrible design.

Was less than a year (10 months) before I got an E63 error with this part. The problem is that the sheet metal in the center is too thin of a gauge and it warped with the continuous temperature cycling. Eventually, the coils contacted the outer housing causing the ground fault (E63).
